# Copilot Instructions for HexMarksTheSpot

> **Keep these instructions up to date.** When implementing new functionality, update this document to reflect the changes — new field types, GUI features, config properties, or architectural decisions. This is the primary context for AI-assisted development.

> **Comment your code.** All non-trivial code should have comments explaining _why_ a decision was made, not just _what_ the code does. This makes enhancements and bug fixes easier to implement correctly.

## Project Overview

HexMarksTheSpot is a Python-based hex file analysis and annotation tool for digital forensics. It parses binary file formats using a declarative JSON configuration language and displays their structure with color-coded hex highlighting, descriptions, and forensic context.

**Modes:** GUI (`gui.py`) and CLI (`main.py --cli <file>`)

## Architecture

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|---------------|
| `common.py` | `Node` dataclass, `FileParser` ABC, `ColorGenerator`, `markdown_to_html()`, exceptions |
| `config_parser.py` | JSON config parser engine — reads `Artefacts/configs/*.json`, parses files into Node trees |
| `cache_manager.py` | SHA-256 file caching (pickle), bookmark persistence (JSON), export (JSON/CSV/Markdown) |
| `parser_loader.py` | `ParserRegistry` singleton, auto-discovery of JSON and Python parsers |
| `gui.py` | Tkinter GUI — hex/ASCII viewer, parsed fields treeview, bookmarks, search, context menus |
| `main.py` | Entry point, CLI interface, `parse_file()` convenience function |

### Data Flow

```
File → ParserRegistry.find_parser_for_file() → Parser.recognizes() → Parser.parse() → Node tree → cache → GUI/CLI
```

### Node Dataclass

```python
@dataclass
class Node:
    data: bytes          # Raw bytes of this segment (b'' for containers)
    info: str            # HTML description (markdown_to_html() output)
    name: str            # Short display name
    color: str           # Hex color (auto-generated by ColorGenerator)
    table_value: Any     # Parsed/interpreted value for table column
    children: List[Tuple[int, Node]]  # (offset, child_node) pairs
```

Container nodes (`struct`, `section`) have `data=b''` to avoid double-counting bytes in hex display. Only leaf fields hold actual bytes.

## Implemented GUI Features

### Layout
- Menu bar (File, Edit, View, Help) — centralizes all actions
- Header with title, 5-column hex/ASCII viewer (offset | hex | ASCII | scrollbar | detail pane)
- Sidebar with parsed fields treeview (Offset, Name, Value columns), search, offset format toggle
- Status bar with progress bar, percentage, timing info

### Menu Bar
- **File:** Open File, Import Hex Text, Export CSV, Export Hex Dump, File Info, Exit
- **Edit:** Copy as Hex/Decimal/ASCII/Parsed Value, Add Bookmark, Bookmarks
- **View:** Toggle Fullscreen
- **Help:** About

### Sidebar Buttons
Open File, Stop Parse (primary actions only — all other actions in menu bar)

### Keyboard Shortcuts
`F11` fullscreen, `Ctrl+Shift+H/D/A/V` copy as hex/decimal/ASCII/parsed value, `Enter` in search field triggers search, `Escape` close modals

### Right-Click Context Menu (parsed fields)
Copy as Hex, Copy as Decimal, Copy as ASCII, Copy Parsed Value, Bookmark

### Bookmarks
- Per-file persistence via `cache_manager` (keyed by SHA-256 hash)
- Bookmark dict: `{name, offset, value, is_raw_hex, comment}`
- Bookmark window: treeview with Name/Offset/Value/Comment, double-click to edit comment, delete, export
- Export formats: JSON (structured metadata), CSV (tabular), Markdown (formatted report with hex display)
- Markdown export: configurable raw hex byte limit (Spinbox dialog), parsed values shown in full, raw hex formatted with spaces/line wraps

### Performance
- Iterative DFS in `_collect_nodes()` (avoids recursion limit)
- Pre-built hex strings via `bytes.hex(' ')`, ASCII via lookup table
- Contrast color caching, pre-computed offsets/values in background thread
- Batched GUI updates (2000 nodes per `after(1)` cycle)
- Pickle-based caching (protocol 5) for parsed Node trees

### Other Features
- Offset format toggle (hex/decimal) with live re-formatting
- Search/filter on field names (Enter key or button)
- File info modal (name, path, size, SHA-256, field count)
- Hex dump export, hex text import (multiple formats)
- Click synchronization between hex viewer and treeview (black border highlight on selected hex bytes and treeview item)
- Hex/ASCII column headers pixel-aligned with content (same font, matched padding)
- Large file warning dialog (>10 MB) before parsing
- Hex integrity safeguard — post-parse verification of parsed bytes vs actual file (count + content), warning dialog on mismatch
- Unparsed gap-fill — hex viewer always shows every byte of the file; byte ranges not covered by any parser field are inserted as "Unparsed Data" entries (light gray) so the hex viewer is the authoritative file view
- Parse logging to `logs/` directory
- Loading overlay with progress estimation

## JSON Parser Configuration Language

Parser configs live in `Artefacts/configs/*.json`. Schema: `parser-config.schema.json`.

### Top-Level Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `$schema` | string | Always `"./parser-config.schema.json"` |
| `name` | string | Format name (required) |
| `description` | string | Format description |
| `magic_bytes` | hex string | File identification bytes (e.g. `"504B0304"`) |
| `magic_offset` | integer | Offset where magic bytes appear (default 0) |
| `endianness` | `"little"` / `"big"` | Default byte order (default `"little"`) |
| `version` | string | Parser version |
| `author` | string | Parser author |
| `references` | string[] | URLs to format documentation |
| `file_extensions` | string[] | File extensions this parser handles (e.g. `[".lnk", ".png"]`) |
| `alternative_magic` | object[] | Alternative magic byte sequences `[{bytes, offset}]` |
| `forensic_notes` | string | Top-level forensic significance description |
| `fields` | field[] | Array of field definitions (required) |

### Parser Matching Precedence

When identifying a file's format, parsers are matched in three tiers:
1. **Extension match** (highest priority) — `file_extensions` match, confirmed by magic bytes
2. **Primary magic bytes** — standard `magic_bytes` at `magic_offset`
3. **Alternative magic bytes** (lowest priority) — `alternative_magic` entries

### Field Types

| Type | Description | Size required? |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| `bytes` | Raw bytes (hex display) | Yes |
| `uint` | Unsigned integer | Yes |
| `int` | Signed integer | Yes |
| `string` | ASCII string | Yes |
| `utf16` / `utf16le` / `utf16be` | UTF-16 encoded string | Yes |
| `guid` | Windows GUID | 16 |
| `filetime` | Windows FILETIME → datetime | 8 |
| `unix_time` | Unix timestamp → datetime | 4 |
| `unix_time_64` | 64-bit Unix timestamp → datetime | 8 |
| `bitfield` | Integer with named bit flags | Yes |
| `vlq` | Variable-Length Quantity (MSB continuation, 1-4 bytes) | No (auto) |
| `skip` | Padding/reserved bytes (skipped in display) | Yes |
| `remaining` | All bytes from current position to EOF | No |
| `struct` | Named container with child `fields` | No |
| `section` | Conditional container with child `fields` | No |

### Field Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Field identifier, used in `$name` references. Must be unique in flat namespace. |
| `size` | int or string | Byte count or expression (`"$field"`, `"$field * 2 - 8"`) |
| `type` | string | One of the field types above |
| `description` | string | Markdown-capable description (bold, italic, code, lists) |
| `endianness` | string | Override for this field (`"little"` / `"big"`) |
| `color` | string | Fixed hex color override (`"#FF0000"`) |
| `condition` | string | Python expression — field is skipped if false |
| `enabled` | bool | `false` to skip entirely (for alternate file structures) |
| `value_map` | object | `{"0": "None", "1": "Document"}` — integer to display name |
| `bit_flags` | object | `{"0": "ReadOnly", "1": "Hidden"}` — bit position to name |
| `expected_values` | array or object | `[512, 1024]` or `{"min": 0, "max": 255}` — validation |
| `forensic_value` | bool or string | `true` or category: `"critical"`, `"important"`, `"timestamp"`, `"identifier"`, `"path"`, `"network"` |
| `informational` | bool | Green/teal highlighting for descriptive fields |
| `deprecated` | bool or string | `true` or reason string — muted gray color, deprecation notice prepended to description |
| `output_format` | string | Display override (see table below) |
| `repeat` | int, string, or `"eof"` / `"until"` | Repeat count, field ref, or mode |
| `repeat_until` | string | Stop condition for `"repeat": "until"` |
| `repeat_step` | int or string | Fixed byte stride per iteration |
| `color_gradient` | bool | Children get progressive lightness variants |
| `fields` | field[] | Child fields for `struct`/`section` |

### Output Format Values

| Format | Example | Use case |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `hex` | `0x0000004C` | Signatures, offsets, flags |
| `decimal` | `16,885,952` | Counts, lengths |
| `ascii` | `MZ` | Magic bytes as text |
| `base64` | `SGVsbG8h` | Binary blobs |
| `binary` | `0b10101011` | Bit patterns |
| `datetime_filetime` | `2023-03-15 14:30:00 UTC` | FILETIME bytes |
| `datetime_unix` | `2019-01-13 08:15:32 UTC` | Unix timestamp bytes |
| `datetime_unix_ms` | `2023-03-15 14:30:00.123 UTC` | Unix ms timestamp |
| `datetime_dos` | `2024-03-15 14:30:00` | DOS/FAT 4-byte timestamp |
| `ip4` | `192.168.1.1` | IPv4 address |
| `ip6` | `2001:0db8:...` | IPv6 address |
| `size_bytes` | `4.0 KB` | Human-readable file sizes |
| `bool` | `True` / `False` | Non-zero = True |

**`type` vs `output_format`:** `type` controls **parsing** (how bytes become a value in `parsed_values`). `output_format` controls **display** only. Don't use `output_format` if the type already displays correctly (e.g., `filetime` already shows a datetime).

### Reference & Expression System

- `$field_name` — resolves to parsed value from the flat `parsed_values` dict
- `$field.N` — bit N of a bitfield (e.g., `$flags.0`)
- Arithmetic: `$header_size - 16`, `$count * 2`
- Conditions: `$type == 5 or $type == 2`, `$flags.0`, `$flags & 0x01`
- Parenthesized expressions: `($field or 65536) - 8` — supports Python ternaries and `or` fallback for default values
- All expressions evaluated via Python `eval()` after `$reference` substitution
- Expressions can start with `(` — the parser detects `$` references anywhere in the string
- VLQ fields auto-store `${name}_bytes` for size tracking

### Repeat Modes

| Mode | Syntax | Behavior |
|------|--------|----------|
| Fixed count | `"repeat": 5` | Exactly 5 iterations |
| Field reference | `"repeat": "$count"` | Value of another field |
| Until EOF | `"repeat": "eof"` | Until file ends |
| Until condition | `"repeat": "until"` + `"repeat_until": "$x == 0"` | Until condition is true |
| With step | `"repeat_step": 1024` | Fixed-size record iteration |

Children are named `Name[0]`, `Name[1]`, etc.

### Color System

Auto-generated by `ColorGenerator` in four categories:
1. **Deprecated** (muted gray) — `deprecated: true` or reason string (highest priority)
2. **Forensic** (red/warm) — `forensic_value: true` or category string
3. **Informational** (green/teal) — `informational: true`
4. **Default** (blue/purple/neutral pastels) — everything else

Adjacent colors guaranteed distinct. `color_gradient: true` creates progressive lightness variants for child fields.

### Common Patterns

```json
// Dynamic-sized field
{ "name": "Data", "size": "$DataLength", "type": "bytes" }

// Conditional section based on flag bit
{ "name": "OptionalData", "type": "section", "condition": "$Flags.0", "fields": [...] }

// Repeat until sentinel
{ "name": "Records", "type": "struct", "repeat": "until",
  "repeat_until": "$Marker == 0", "fields": [...] }

// Type dispatch (read type, then conditional sections)
{ "name": "AttrType", "size": 4, "type": "int" },
{ "name": "TypeA", "type": "section", "condition": "$AttrType == 16", "fields": [...] },
{ "name": "TypeB", "type": "section", "condition": "$AttrType == 48", "fields": [...] }
```

### Important Notes

- `parsed_values` is a **flat dict** — field names from nested structs share the same namespace. Use prefixed names to avoid collisions (e.g., `SI_CreationTime`, `FN_CreationTime`).
- Container nodes (`struct`, `section`) have `data=b''` — only leaf fields hold actual bytes.
- The `remaining` type reads to EOF — use only at the end of a parser.
- `enabled: false` completely skips a field — useful for documenting alternate file structures.
- Descriptions support markdown: `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `\n\n` paragraphs, `- item` / `1. item` lists.

## Caching System

- SHA-256 hash keyed, stored at `cache/<hash>/` with `parsed.pkl`, `meta.json`, `bookmarks.json`
- Pickle protocol 5 (fast), with legacy JSON fallback + auto-upgrade
- Bookmarks persisted per-file as JSON, exported as JSON/CSV/Markdown

## Converting 010 Editor Templates (.bt)

`.bt` files in `Artefacts/` are reference specs. Type mappings: `char[N]` → `string`, `short`/`ushort` → `uint` (2), `int`/`uint` → `uint`/`int` (4), `int64` → `uint` (8), `FILETIME` → `filetime`, `wchar_t[N]` → `utf16le`. Convert `if` → `condition`, `while`/`for` → `repeat`, enums → `value_map` or `bitfield`.

## Quality Standards

1. Include `$schema` reference
2. Document every field with `description` (forensic context where relevant)
3. Add `forensic_notes` at parser level
4. Mark forensic fields with appropriate categories
5. Add `references` with specification URLs
6. Use `expected_values` for known-valid ranges
7. Use `value_map` for enum-like fields
8. Account for all bytes (use `skip` for padding)
9. Test with real files in `TestFiles/`

## Reference Parsers

- **`sqlite.json`** — Big-endian, extensive `expected_values`, `enabled: false` for WAL/journal, structured page content (CellPointerArray, UnallocatedSpace, CellContentArea per page), parenthesized expressions for default values (`$field or 65536`)
- **`lnk_shell_link.json`** — Complex conditionals, `forensic_notes`, `repeat: "until"`, deeply nested
- **`mft.json`** — Type-dispatched attributes, prefixed field names, timestomping documentation
- **`prefetch.json`** — Multi-version with conditions, full metrics/chains/volume parsing

## File Structure

```
HexMarksTheSpot/
├── gui.py               # Tkinter GUI application
├── main.py              # CLI entry point
├── common.py            # Node, FileParser, ColorGenerator, exceptions
├── config_parser.py     # JSON config parser engine
├── cache_manager.py     # Pickle caching, bookmark persistence, export
├── parser_loader.py     # Auto-discovery, ParserRegistry singleton
├── Artefacts/
│   ├── *.bt             # 010 Editor templates (reference)
│   └── configs/
│       ├── parser-config.schema.json
│       ├── _template.json
│       └── *.json       # Active parser configs
├── TestFiles/           # Sample files for testing
└── images/              # GUI assets
```
